# Corridor pull readiness — where new properties can actually come from

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/corridor_readiness.py from market/corridors.json.
     Do not edit: run the script. tests/run.py fails the build if it is stale. -->

"Add more properties to the corridors" is 24 different jobs. This page is the
ordered answer, read out of the `parcel` block each metro already carries in
[`market/corridors.json`](../market/corridors.json) — the endpoint that was probed
and what came back. Nothing here is a new claim; the verdicts are the prober's own.

The development container reaches none of these hosts — every route is
policy-blocked, re-probed and dated in
[`states/coverage/README.md`](states/coverage/README.md#egress-routes-dated) — so the
pull runs over the desktop browser pane per [`PULL_RECIPE.md`](PULL_RECIPE.md).
This page decides where that session spends its time.

## The count

| Tier | Corridors |
|---|---|
| Ready to pull | **14** |
| Ready, with a caveat recorded | **1** |
| Usable in part | **2** |
| Endpoint works, roll does not | **1** |
| No public parcel roll | **1** |
| Never probed | **5** |
| **Total** | **24** |

**15 of 24 corridors can gain properties from a session that starts today.**
The 5 never probed are the cheapest place to grow that number, because a single
endpoint check either adds a corridor or records an honest blocker.

Of those, **5 corridors recorded an actual parcel count** when probed, and they
total **571,912 parcels**. That is the measured size of what a pull session could
add from the endpoints already confirmed — not an estimate, and not a promise
that every parcel clears a screen; it is the count the services themselves
returned. The rest answered without stating a total.

Every one of those counted corridors is in **LA**, which puts the largest
confirmed block of pullable parcels in the same state as the New Orleans
editions — one jurisdiction’s use-code vocabulary to map, reused across all
of them. That is the cheapest path from a confirmed endpoint to a screened
property this file offers.

## What this page does not say

It does not say how many parcels any endpoint holds — only the notes that
recorded a count say that, and they say it in their own words. It does not rank
corridors by how attractive they are; that is what the belt ranking and the
corridor scores are for. And a "ready" verdict is a verdict about the *endpoint*,
not about the use-class vocabulary behind it: a pulled roll still has to clear
[`crosswalk/validate_usecodes.py`](../crosswalk/validate_usecodes.py) before any
property it carries can be screened by class.
